RESOLVED (was: alignment.py's own module docstring cited 'jumped'/'panted' as words that resolve through the inflectional-endings suffix path, but they actually resolve to consonant_blends via their stems' final blend). This was a doc bug, not a code bug - classify_skill_for_word('jumped') == 'consonant_blends' was already the intended, tested behavior (tests/test_skills.py already asserted it). Fixed by correcting the docstring's example words in backend/tutor/skills.py to match reality (helped/filled for the pure-suffix case, barked/jumped for the stem-has-its-own-pattern case) rather than changing any classification logic.

PARTIALLY RESOLVED (was: open_syllables at 11%, 1/9): classify_skill_for_word's open-syllable check used to only test whether the whole word's LAST letter is a vowel. Replaced with a VCV structural check (single medial consonant between two vowels, e.g. 'ti-ny', 'ro-bot') in backend/tutor/skills.py, verified against the full tutor-logic test suite (35/35 still passing) before and after. This category is now 66.7% (6/9). Three words remain known, deliberately unfixed gaps, each re-asserted explicitly in tests/test_skills.py so a future change notices if the behavior shifts: 'tiger'/'hero' are caught earlier by the r_controlled_vowels whole-word substring scan (same 'er' shape as a real same-syllable case like 'sister'), and 'apron' has a two-consonant medial blend ('pr') that's genuinely ambiguous without a pronouncing dictionary - the same blend shape closes the syllable in a short-vowel word ('bas-ket', 'gob-lin') but stays open in a long-vowel one ('a-pron', 'ze-bra'); an earlier, more aggressive version of this fix treated any medial blend as open and wrongly flipped 'basket'/'goblin' to open_syllables as a result, so that path was deliberately left out rather than traded for a new regression.
